newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto "detention" challenged in Pakistan court.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto "detention" challenged in Pakistan court.

text.p: Lawyers filed a petition in a Pakistani court on Tuesday claiming that ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto had been illegally detained, court sources said.
The lawyers, acting for dismissed defence minister Aftab Shaaban Meerani, filed the habeas corpus petition before the Lahore High Court's bench in Rawalpindi city, near Islamabad.
The court issued a notice to the secretary of the Interior Ministry and set the hearing for Wednesday, the sources said.
No more details were immediately available.
Bhutto has been held virtually incommunicado at her official residence in Islamabad since President Farooq Leghari issued a proclamation dismissing her in the early hours.
But troops guarding the prime minister's house allowed the chief minister of North West Frontier Province, Aftab Sherpao, to visit her on Tuesday afternoon, witnesses said.
He was the first Bhutto loyalist known to have gained access to her.

Sherpao, who belongs to Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party, earlier visited Leghari, who also dissolved the National Assembly (lower house) and appointed a caretaker premier to oversee snap elections on February 3, 1997.
Leghari accused Bhutto's government of fostering corruption, undermining the judiciary and failing to stop extra-judicial killings in Karachi and elsewhere.

Former government ministers who tried to see Bhutto earlier in the day said they were turned back by police posted near her residence, an elegant white two-storey house on a low hill overlooking a sprawl of government buildings.
